Review V2 - (Near the end of the first DLC)

I wanted to rewrite my review of this game after having finished the game, but also having replayed about 60 missions on Hardest and attempting the first mission pack on Hardest too, so I have been able to understand what the later game may look like in Earth Defence Force V. This will be spoiler free for most of the games content. 

Earth Defence Force V is the epitome of power fantasy, however in a much rarer form, in that of the boots of a soldier on the grounds of a war waged between an invasive alien species and the newly formed Earth Defence Force. If one deigns to categorise this game and associate it other titles, then the closest you are able will be 'horde shooter'. However, I believe this is a poor categorisation as it differs so much to other games in this genre like Deep Rock or Helldivers (though Helldivers 2 is probably the best thing you've got in terms of similarity, if talking about another series). 

Earth Defence Force's general gameplay loop involves fighting off huge amounts of gargantuan aliens of many different varieties. These aliens are usually the size of a 2 story building and will be extremely aggressive. Fear not, as you have four mighty classes and an even mightier arsenal supporting your endeavour against the aliens who invaded. To find out what you are, see below:

1. Ranger - The classic all-arounder who excels in using precision and non-precision weapons of all aspects. If this is your first class I highly recommend you try Ranger for a few missions to understand the general loop of the game. As ranger you can involve yourself in AI squad play, a variety of weapons to suit distances and aliens.

2. Air Raider - My favourite, and as the name implies, uses the air as a means to rain hell onto the ground. This class is based around explosives and technology, but also various devastating vehicles and airstrikes which can absolute destroy friend or foe. 

3. Wing Diver - A class with high skill expression and agility. You don a jetpack and your fuel is rechargeable - however all movements using your jetpack and reloading/charging your weapons will use the same fuel. Mastering this balance will allow you to wreak absolutely gargantuan amounts of damage whilst mitigating the damage done to your small health pool.

4. Fencer - A jack of all trades like the ranger, but I think lacks the pinpoint precision and simplicity ranger can bring to the stage. Fencer is equipped with an exosuit that can be augumented with various speed, boost and ability upgrades which will compliment your weapons which tend to lean towards larger weapons that you may find on a vehicle. Artillery cannons, large miniguns, hammers, blades, shields and more will be strapped to your exosuit as you slowly move around the map between your extremely agile dashes and dash-jumps you can use.

Between all these 4 classes there must be at least 1500 weapons available in the game. The replayability of this game is amazing, with new weapons and upgrades getting introduced in harder difficulties. The light but extremely entertaining cast, voice actors and story means the gameplay is the true focus for players of this title. This gameplay, amongst the many weapons and variety of classes, is complimented via the wide assortment of enemies, maps and scenarios you get thrust into (especially for the DLC). Whilst this game may seem like absolute chaos looking at it, there is a huge amount of strategy and thinking that will go on, especially if you have 2 players. 

There was many times (especially in the DLC and later campaign) where I had to switch my loadout various times and play particular ways with the environment to give ourside the edge over the aliens who have very distinct powers and AI which make fighting each one engage you and your loadout much more than other games. 

I'll leave it there but just know that EDF 5 is an absolute gem when it comes to the traditional horde shooter game genre. If you have a stack of 2 to 4, I highly recommend you lockin to EDF as a type of party game initially, blowing each other up and enjoying the carnage on screen. As you warm up to the game and the classes, the game will start to inject difficulty into the game in which you can really engage yourselves but also have a fun in a different way to than you did initially (if you are sceptical about the game). It has easily 100s of hours of replayability and if you are willing to give it a go you may find yourself enamoured. My main complaint is the notorious box collection system. 

Do yourself a favour and have everyone download the mod that picks up all item boxes at the end of a 
mission. Some people enjoy the cycle of collecting boxes to unlock Max HP and new weapons, but I think it becomes extremely tedious. With this mod , when the mission ends you can jump in a vehicle during the 'mission complete' splashscreen which will pick up every box on the map ensuring you dont lose masses of new weapons or max HP increases for your classes.
